name: Flaxseed lignan (secoisolariciresinol diglucoside)
short: Placebo-controlled trials up to 12 months (older adults, women at raised breast cancer risk, men with enlarged prostate): adverse events not more common. One trial: no low blood sugar or pressure.
text: These sources concern lignan extracts of flaxseed (secoisolariciresinol diglucoside, SDG), not whole flaxseed or flaxseed oil. In a 12-month randomized placebo-controlled phase IIB trial in 180 premenopausal women at increased risk of breast cancer, 50 mg of SDG daily had a similar adverse event incidence to placebo, with no evidence of harm. In a 6-month randomized double-blind placebo-controlled trial in healthy adults aged 60 to 80, a flaxseed lignan-enriched complex taken by mouth once daily produced no reported adverse effects and no differences from placebo in blood biochemistry or lipids, although in lignan-takers whose systolic blood pressure was 140 mm Hg or higher it fell significantly, from a mean of 155 to 140 mm Hg at 24 weeks (the abstract does not say how this compared with placebo); in a separate 6-month randomized double-blind trial in adults aged 49 to 87 (94 completers), a flaxseed lignan product caused no episodes of low blood sugar or low blood pressure. In an 8-week randomized placebo-controlled pilot trial in men with benign prostatic hyperplasia, a lignan-rich flaxseed hull extract did not lead to adverse effects compared with placebo. These trials were small to moderate in size and the abstracts do not report long-term data beyond 12 months. No interaction data were found in the cited sources.
